inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,705 logical lines. The article develops modified Mellin transforms of zeta moments, especially Z₂(s), and connects their analytic and mean-square behavior to the fourth-moment error E₂(T), higher zeta moments, the hyperbolic spectral decomposition, and weighted sums of central Hecke values. It proves transform lemmas, unconditional lower/upper and interpolation-type bounds, proposes three distinct conjectures with traced consequences, derives a new pointwise bound away from poles through a refined saddle analysis, and generalizes the framework to Z_k(s). Twenty-six units preserve exact results, conditional implications, and explicitly heuristic routes without conflating them. Formula extraction is materially degraded throughout: integral signs and comparison symbols disappear, exponents and ranges drift vertically, and some saddle expressions contain control artifacts, so exact statements and constants require PDF verification even when the prose mechanism is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Maass spectral data packages central Hecke values into a positive weighted family
accepted_units.why_material: The paper fixes Laplacian eigenvalues, simultaneous Hecke eigenforms, parity, and their Hecke series, creating the spectral coordinates later visible as poles and exponential sums. This setup explains why central Hecke values, rather than arbitrary coefficients, control fourth-moment phenomena.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the operator/eigenbasis definitions and Hecke-series normalization needed for every later spectral formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Operator sums, eigenvalue normalization, and Dirichlet-series ranges are formula-sensitive and vertically fragmented; verify exact normalizations from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Poles of Z₂ encode the hyperbolic spectrum and central Hecke values
accepted_units.why_material: The modified Mellin transform of the fourth zeta moment has a meromorphic continuation whose off-real poles occur at spectral parameters, with residues weighted by cubes of central Hecke values; additional poles track zeta zeros. This makes Z₂ a bridge between moment errors and spectral cancellation.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the positivity/average input, definition, singularity list, residue description, and the author’s section roadmap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform definition is clear, but residue gamma factors, multiplicities, conjugations, and comparison symbols are damaged; exact residue use requires PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Modified Mellin inversion avoids the origin while retaining ordinary Mellin structure
accepted_units.why_material: A reflection-and-truncation device identifies the modified transform over [1,∞) with an ordinary Mellin transform, transferring Fourier/Mellin inversion to recover the original function under explicit integrability and continuity conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the ordinary Fourier correspondence, inversion/Parseval context, modified definition, and proof of the first inversion lemma.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour notation, powers, Lᵖ conditions, and reflected arguments are displaced in extraction. The functional relationship is readable, but exact hypotheses and inversion powers require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Products in the original variable become transform convolution and Parseval identities
accepted_units.why_material: Two lemmas transfer the ordinary Mellin product formula and Parseval identity to the modified transform, supplying both a convolution law and an exact weighted L² identity. These become the algebraic engine for later moment and recurrence arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: The proofs are retained because the shift s+1−w and weight x^{1−2σ} arise from the reflection defining the modified transform.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several conjugation bars, line integrals, weights, and L² conditions are not reliably placed; all exact identities and domains should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Localization and contour shifting transfer transform mean squares back to the source function
accepted_units.why_material: A localized Parseval inequality bounds the mean square of a truncated modified transform by a weighted source norm. A converse-style lemma then smooths a dyadic source interval, shifts past the transform’s polar part, truncates by repeated integration by parts, and uses Cauchy–Schwarz plus Parseval to control the source mean square by the transform mean square.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines Lemmas 4–5 because the later lower-bound argument uses their forward/backward transfer as one mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula risk: missing comparison symbols, shifted integration limits, contour indentation, polynomial degree wording, derivative indices, and T-exponents make exact bounds unsafe without the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fourth-moment error bounds set the attainable scale for Z₂ mean squares
accepted_units.why_material: The section defines E₂(T), inventories its mean-square, pointwise, omega, and integral behavior, and records how an assumed pointwise exponent for E₂ feeds an existing Z₂ mean-square estimate. This establishes the unconditional baseline and identifies which scales are already essentially optimal.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the fourth-moment polynomial definition and all compared estimates because later conjectures are calibrated against them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many big-O/omega/comparison glyphs are absent, and logarithmic powers and exponent ranges drift. Exact bound directions and constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Removing the polar part makes E₂ and Z₂ mean squares Parseval dual
accepted_units.why_material: Integration by parts decomposes Z₂ into an explicit pole at one plus the transform of E₂. After subtracting the polar part, Parseval gives an exact weighted identity; contour propagation then shows that a boundary Z₂ mean-square bound recovers the best known E₂ and twelfth-moment estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the reverse implication and consequences to show why Z₂ mean-square control is not merely a reformulation but a high-leverage target.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Polar coefficients, gamma-kernel contour, rectangle vertices, and several T/X exponents are extraction-sensitive. Verify exact equivalences and allowable σ-ranges from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A source-to-transform transfer forces a lower bound for every interior Z₂ mean square
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 applies the mean-square transfer lemma to Hardy’s real Z-function: a known lower bound for the eighth zeta moment cannot be supported unless the Z₂ transform has at least the stated mean-square size. This supplies evidence that the later conjectured exponent is sharp from below.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the derivative control needed to verify the transfer lemma’s hypotheses and the substitution converting the long transform interval to the theorem’s scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Riemann–Siegel derivative formula and the final exponents contain severe layout loss. The logic is recoverable, but the exact lower bound, ε placement, and log powers require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: A smoothed Mellin decomposition propagates Z₂ control between vertical lines
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 partitions the transform into low, middle, and tail ranges, handles the tail via E₂ and localized Parseval, reinserts Z₂ by Mellin inversion on the middle range, and truncates the resulting convolution by repeated integration by parts. The result is a convexity-type mean-square and pointwise transfer from a line c to a line σ.
accepted_units.context_note: The long proof is retained as a reusable analytic mechanism: smooth partition, polar subtraction, contour displacement, frequency localization, then Cauchy–Schwarz.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-dependent: cutoff supports, line shifts, nested integration limits, maxima over dyadic K, and exponents are heavily fragmented. Only the strategy is safe until formulas (3.23)–(3.28) are checked from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrapping the propagation theorem sharpens mean-square bounds near σ=1
accepted_units.why_material: Feeding a previously known estimate on one vertical line into Theorem 2 yields an improved exponent for σ at least 5/6, demonstrating how the transfer inequality can bootstrap existing information.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the comparison with the prior bound to make the region of genuine improvement explicit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The σ thresholds and exponents are readable but densely typeset; verify their exact values and ε terms from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 1 posits the lower-bound scale and would optimize E₂ and the eighth moment
accepted_units.why_material: The proposed Z₂ mean-square bound matches Theorem 1’s scale up to ε. A smoothed inverse-transform argument would then give square-root-size E₂, while the earlier transfer inequality would give the conjecturally optimal eighth moment.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both corollary proofs so the conditional arrows are explicit rather than inferred from similarity of exponents.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Smoothing supports, contour truncation, H choice, and exact exponent arithmetic are extraction-sensitive. These are conditional deductions, not observed evidence.

accepted_units.title: The eighth-moment conjecture is equivalent to a weaker piecewise Z₂ mean-square bound
accepted_units.why_material: The paper cannot prove equivalence with Conjecture 1 itself, but shows that the optimal eighth moment yields a piecewise transform estimate and that the near-one portion of that estimate recovers the eighth moment. This precisely locates the gap between a desired conjecture and a provably equivalent surrogate.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the author’s explicit weakening to avoid overstating the conjectural relationship.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The piecewise cases and their σ ranges are visually compressed; exact exponents must be PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 2 is a Lindelöf-type pointwise claim equivalent to vertical decay
accepted_units.why_material: A pointwise subpower conjecture for Z₂ is reformulated as the stronger-looking decay t^{1/2−σ+ε}. The proof shows self-improvement: smooth truncation, contour shift to near the critical line, and a second integral representation convert the original uniform bound into decay across the strip.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the analogy with classical Lindelöf and the full equivalence argument; it also records that Conjecture 2 immediately implies Conjecture 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Cutoff derivatives, contour L, maximum ranges, and final exponent balancing are badly line-broken. Verify the exact scope, especially distance from poles and σ ranges, from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: RH, Lindelöf, E₂, and eighth-moment implications are not interchangeable
accepted_units.why_material: The author explicitly warns that the optimal E₂ bound and eighth-moment bound do not appear to imply one another, and that RH does not apparently yield the former even though Lindelöf yields the latter. This prevents collapsing distinct conjectural channels.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained as a high-value logical boundary; the line’s internal reference to Lindelöf is typographically ambiguous, so only the prose distinction is used.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: A cross-reference appears inconsistent in the extraction. Verify the cited equation number from the PDF before quoting; do not treat the passage as a new proof.

accepted_units.title: Central Hecke values require cancellation beyond positive short-interval bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The section compares Lindelöf-type cancellation in ordinary Dirichlet sums with central Hecke-value sums. Known positivity gives strong average and pointwise bounds but cannot improve an unweighted unit spectral interval; inserting an oscillatory phase is therefore identified as the missing source of square-root cancellation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the ordinary exponential-sum analogy, conjectural Hecke size, known short-interval theorem, and the transition from unweighted to weighted sums.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several comparison signs and exponents in (5.1)–(5.7) are missing or displaced. Exact known and conjectural strengths require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Two zeta problems reduce to the same oscillatory spectral phase
accepted_units.why_material: Both E₂ and the eighth moment are expressed through short spectral sums weighted by central Hecke values. Absolute-value use of the known bound is too weak; Stirling asymptotics of the residue factor exposes an oscillatory phase, revealing that both applications demand essentially the same cancellation problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains both application formulas, the failed absolute estimate, and phase extraction so the conjecture that follows is problem-driven rather than decorative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This span is highly formula-sensitive: Gaussian weights, supremum ranges, residue gamma factors, support intervals, and oscillatory phases are degraded. Exact reductions require checking formulas (5.8)–(5.15) in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Conjecture 3 posits square-root cancellation in unit spectral intervals
accepted_units.why_material: The conjecture asks an oscillatory unit-interval sum of positive central Hecke weights to save a square root over the best unweighted bound. The paper traces this hypothesis separately to optimal E₂ and eighth-moment bounds, noting an additional spectral-error step needed for the latter.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both conditional corollaries and their proof sketches, preserving the caveat that the eighth-moment remainder must also be controlled.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The phase parameter range, square-root exponent, partial-summation weights, and error-term notation are extraction-sensitive. All consequences remain conditional on Conjecture 3.

accepted_units.title: Motohashi’s transformation formula offers a smoothed route but not the unsmoothed target
accepted_units.why_material: The author proposes embedding the unit-interval exponential sum in a spectral transformation formula with an even Gaussian-localized test function and adjustable window G. The key obstruction is explicit: progress for the Gaussian-smoothed transform would not automatically control the unsmoothed sum required by the zeta applications.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the test-function design and the failure-of-transfer warning as a concrete research route with a stated limitation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The test function’s polynomial prefactor, phase, Gaussian windows, and admissible strip are densely damaged; exact implementation requires the PDF and cited transformation formula.

accepted_units.title: Any one of the three conjectures yields a strengthened zeta-weighted Dirichlet-polynomial mean value
accepted_units.why_material: The paper identifies a shared downstream inequality for arbitrary Dirichlet coefficients and compares it with prior unconditional bounds, showing that the conjectures control more than the motivating E₂ and moment problems.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the comparison and Selberg-eigenvalue caveat to distinguish the conditional improvement from the known method’s limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The N/T range, coefficient norm, and competing exponents are line-broken; verify the exact statement of (5.18) before use.

accepted_units.title: Spectral residues heuristically link Conjecture 3 to Conjecture 2 and motivate a new unconditional bound
accepted_units.why_material: Shifting a contour across Z₂’s spectral poles predicts a short residue sum. Ignoring its oscillation and using only the known average gives t^{1−σ+ε}; using Conjecture 3 would give the pointwise conjecture. The article then isolates the former as a theorem away from poles.
accepted_units.context_note: Explicitly separates the heuristic residue calculation from the rigorously stated Theorem 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Residue kernels, localization width, X powers, and the meaning of ‘well separated’ are not quantified reliably in extraction; consult the PDF and cited source for the exact hypothesis.

accepted_units.title: Oscillation removes an artificial smoothing-width restriction in the pointwise bound
accepted_units.why_material: The proof revisits a spectral decomposition based on a Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment. A previous saddle estimate required ξ≥1/3; expanding the saddle more accurately, isolating the phase derivative, and applying a first-derivative test controls the formerly troublesome contribution for every positive ξ, permitting ξ≈0 and yielding the claimed pointwise exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the alternative route through Motohashi’s kernel, the chosen direct modification, saddle expansion, phase-derivative argument, pole-separation use, and extension of the σ-range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme formula risk: the hypergeometric kernel, saddle equation, z₀ expansion, G(z₀), phase derivatives, and integration ranges contain missing symbols and displaced powers. The conceptual correction is recoverable, but the proof cannot be reconstructed safely without the PDF and cited predecessor.

accepted_units.title: Any pointwise improvement for Z₂ propagates quantitatively to E₂ and zeta moments
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem’s boundary value recovers known mean-square and moment bounds; more generally, a hypothetical exponent ρ for Z₂ gives an explicit improved exponent for E₂. This quantifies why spectral exponential-sum progress is the bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the parametric exponent relation rather than only the special current bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-root display, ρ notation, and rational exponent are extraction-sensitive; verify formula (6.15) exactly from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation of every Z_k is equivalent to the Lindelöf moment hierarchy
accepted_units.why_material: Mellin inversion converts smoothed 2k-th zeta moments into contour integrals of Z_k. Regular polynomial-growth continuation just beyond σ=1 implies all Lindelöf-strength moments, while integration by parts gives the converse; taken over all k, this is equivalent to Lindelöf.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both directions and the quantification over k so a weak single-k statement is not mistaken for full equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Order of integration, smoothing assumptions, contour position, and σ inequalities are partially scrambled. The equivalence claim is readable but exact analytic hypotheses require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Z₁ satisfies the conjectured mean-square scale but not the pointwise analogue
accepted_units.why_material: The k=1 transform already has the mean-square exponent conjectured for Z₂ and a dyadic refinement, yet its Lindelöf-type pointwise bound remains out of reach. This demonstrates that mean-square success does not automatically resolve pointwise control even in the simpler case.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the lower-bound optimality comment and the sharper dyadic form as calibration for Conjectures 1–2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The σ ranges, plus T⁻¹ term, and comparison directions require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Products of zeta moments induce a convolution recurrence among Z_k
accepted_units.why_material: Double Mellin inversion expresses a 2(k+l)-th moment through Z_k and Z_l with frequency coupling, while the modified-transform convolution lemma gives a direct recurrence Z_{k+l} as a vertical convolution. This suggests building higher-moment information compositionally from lower transforms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the localized triple-integral viewpoint and the concise recurrence because they show respectively the frequency constraint and the algebraic structure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested contours, powers, variables, and convergence conditions are heavily line-broken. Treat the recurrence’s exact shift and contour as PDF-dependent.

accepted_units.title: The eighth moment heuristically forces Conjecture 3’s square-root scale
accepted_units.why_material: Taking k=l=2 in the transform factorization and isolating the discrete spectral contribution turns the known eighth-moment lower scale into a lower bound for a supremum of the same short oscillatory Hecke sums. After truncation and Stirling analysis, this argues that Conjecture 3 would be essentially optimal.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly heuristic: it uses the conjectured pointwise control to truncate and then performs trivial supremum extraction; it is not a proof of the lower bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The supremum range, phase constant, spectral localization, nested integral, and final exponent are degraded. Exact formulation (7.8) and every heuristic transition require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The transform–error–moment triangle
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Modified Mellin inversion and Parseval make three forms of control mutually informative: analytic/mean-square bounds for Z₂, size of the fourth-moment error E₂, and higher zeta moments. Smoothing and polar subtraction determine which implications are exact, conditional, or lossy.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The arrows are not all equivalences: the paper explicitly identifies gaps, and exact exponent transfer depends on formula-sensitive hypotheses.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral poles become a cancellation bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Residues of Z₂ at spectral poles expose positive central Hecke weights; unweighted estimates saturate, while Stirling analysis reveals an oscillatory phase whose square-root cancellation would simultaneously improve E₂, the eighth moment, and pointwise Z₂.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The square-root cancellation is Conjecture 3, and the route from it to all stated applications includes conditional or heuristic steps.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A hierarchy of non-equivalent conjectural strengths
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The article distinguishes a mean-square conjecture for Z₂, a stronger pointwise Lindelöf analogue, a spectral exponential-sum conjecture, optimal moment statements, and classical RH/Lindelöf; several one-way implications are proved, but equivalence is established only for narrower reformulations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a dependency map within the source, not evidence that any of Conjectures 1–3 is true.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Smoothing creates tractability but can hide the target oscillation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smooth cutoffs enable contour shifts, frequency truncation, and saddle estimates throughout the paper, yet the proposed spectral transformation illustrates that a Gaussian-smoothed bound need not transfer to the unsmoothed unit-window sum actually required.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The boundary between removable smoothing and essential unsmoothed control is source-specific and depends on unverified dense formulas.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A recursive calculus for moment transforms
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The convolution law makes Z_{k+l} compositional in Z_k and Z_l, while localized inversion reveals coupled spectral frequencies; this lets low-order transform information diagnose both higher moments and the plausible optimal scale of spectral cancellation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Convergence contours and pointwise inputs are essential, and the final optimality argument is explicitly heuristic.

stop_reason: All 1,705 logical lines were inspected from spectral definitions through the general Z_k framework. The plan represents every distinct transform identity, unconditional theorem, conjecture, proved conditional implication, proposed route, obstruction, and heuristic optimality argument. Remaining lines are journal/front matter, section separators, running headers embedded in covered spans, bibliography, or author metadata; further segmentation would repeat represented calculations or claim exactness unsupported by the damaged formula extraction.
